result.title: Auditing Future-Memory Use in Point-in-Time Language Agents
result.summary: Point-in-time (PIT) agents can recall post-cutoff facts even when their external evidence respects a historical cutoff. We examine whether this access predicts evidence gathering in 48 historical company-comparison tasks. Independent closed-book revenue probes identify the better-remembered company for each model on tasks with unequal recall, fixing the predicted direction before agent runs. We then compare paired runs with real or anonymized company identities while keeping external evidence PIT-valid. Both Qwen and DeepSeek recalled future facts, but neither supported the prespecified shift toward the better-remembered company. Qwen's four allocation estimates on 28 unequal-recall tasks were negative, with descriptive intervals spanning zero. A prospective DeepSeek replication showed an inverse pattern across all four metrics on 20 such tasks, with intervals below zero. These estimates remained negative after each company, pair, and future-fact omission, and all four post-hoc max-T-adjusted sign-flip p-values were below .05. In a prospectively specified follow-up, explicit future facts produced small estimated shifts away from the supplied-fact company, with intervals spanning zero, while final choices shifted toward it. The mechanism behind the natural inverse pattern remains unresolved. These findings support separate assessments of memory accessibility, search allocation, and final outputs alongside cutoff checks on external evidence.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在 48 个历史公司比较任务上审计 point-in-time 智能体：用闭卷收入探针预先确定「记忆更好的公司」，再以真实/匿名身份配对运行并保持外部证据符合历史截断，检验参数记忆中的未来事实是否真的改变证据收集与最终选择；结果两家模型都记得未来事实，却未出现预设方向的偏移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把「记忆可访问性—搜索分配—最终输出」分开审计的做法，以及匿名化配对、前设方向预测的设计，可能为核查 LVR 中 latent 内容是否被答案真正使用、视觉旁路与贡献分配提供方法线索，可供人工核查。
